Aelsin Ube-Coconut Mood Pearls#

Small, spherical hard candies with an ube-violet shell encasing a liquid coconut center dosed with low-grade anxiolytic bioactive compounds. Sold in apothecary-style glass vials of fifteen.
candymoodcandy hard candyconsumer_goodgenewarecorporatecontrolmarkettier 3tier 4
name Aelsin Ube-Coconut Mood Pearls
brand name Aelsin
product name Aelsin Ube-Coconut Mood Pearls
category candy
subcategory mood-candy / hard candy
manufacturer Aelsin Wellness Confections
flavor profile Sweet, earthy ube dissolving into a cool coconut cream with a subtle warmth as the bioactive compound takes effect — mild calm onset within twelve minutes
tier availability Tier 3-4
price Φ11.00
popularity rank 16
slogan Calm, not numb.
cultural context Aelsin Mood Pearls occupy a precise market niche: legal, mild emotional modulation for Tier 3-4 consumers who want something more discreet than a prescription and more effective than tea. The glass vial packaging is considered elegant and is frequently reused for storing jewelry, micro-components, or other small valuables.
story hooks
  • Aelsin's anxiolytic compound is derived from a geneware-modified plant strain that a Tier 1 botanist developed and never received credit or compensation for — she wants the formula, the credit, or both.
  • A Tier 4 corporate negotiator has been secretly dosing a rival's coffee with crushed Mood Pearls before high-stakes meetings — the rival has noticed they feel unusually compliant but can't pinpoint why.
  • The GLMZ Pharmacological Oversight Bureau is preparing to reclassify Mood Pearls as a controlled substance; Aelsin's lobbyists are scrambling, and the company needs public-facing allies fast.

Aelvar Cloudberry-Oolong Frost#

A chilled tea soda made with real oolong extract and synth-cloudberry flavoring, lightly sparkling. Aelvar is a licensed boutique label under a larger corponation umbrella, given creative freedom to maintain its craft credibility.

story hooks
  • Aelvar's parent corponation is planning to reformulate the product with cheaper synth-oolong, and an Aelvar brand manager is considering leaking the plan to protect the label's reputation.
  • A food critic's damning review of Aelvar went viral and then quietly disappeared — someone pulled it, and the critic wants to know who.
  • A case of Aelvar was found at a crime scene with no explanation for how it got there — it's a Tier 3-4 product in a Tier 1 location.
